trait.text: a way of rocking on the heels
pay: {person.He} went on rocking on {person.his} heels. I got the feeling I’d been considered, and filed with the weather.

text: {He} had the look of a {man} who had sat in the same seat so long it had given up and taken {his} shape.

trait.text: the look of somebody who had sat in the same seat so long it had taken their shape
pay: The seat had {person.his} shape, and the night had mine. Neither of us was getting up soon.

text: {He} had the radio going low and an opinion about every fare of the evening.

trait.text: the radio going low, and an opinion about every fare
pay: The radio was still going low. By now I had my place in the evening’s opinions, somewhere between the drunk and the one who didn’t tip.

text: {He} looked at me in the mirror first, from habit, before turning round.

trait.text: a look in the mirror first, from habit
pay: I caught {person.him} looking at me in the mirror again, from habit. It’s the only way some people look at anybody.

text: {He} had the look of a {man} who knew what everybody on the street was taking and why.

trait.text: the look of somebody who knew what everybody on the street was taking and why
pay: {person.He} knew what everybody on the street was taking. I hoped nobody had asked about me.

text: {He} peered at me over {his} spectacles with the caution of somebody who has to sign for things.

trait.text: a way of peering over the spectacles, with the caution of somebody who signs for things
pay: {person.He} looked at me over the spectacles one more time, the way you look at something before you sign for it. I didn’t get signed for.

text: {He} had a clean white coat and a quiet voice that {he} never raised above the price of aspirin.

trait.text: a quiet voice never raised above the price of aspirin
pay: The quiet voice never went above the price of aspirin. By then I needed some.

text: {He} had the look of somebody who had been having a long night before I got there.

trait.text: the look of somebody who had been having a long night before I got there
pay: I hadn’t made {person.his} night any shorter. I rarely do that for anybody, me included.

text: {He} looked at me with the polite dread people keep for detectives and dentists.

trait.text: the polite dread people keep for detectives and dentists
pay: The polite dread never quite went away. I don’t blame anybody. I feel the same about dentists.

text: {He} had a face that was trying hard to look as if it had nothing to do with anything.

trait.text: a face trying hard to look as if it had nothing to do with anything
pay: The face was still trying hard to have nothing to do with anything. Most faces do, around me.

text: {He} gave me the same look as before, only less of it.
{He} didn’t sigh, but {he} let me watch {him} decide not to.
{He} waited, which with {him} was most of the conversation.
{He} had the patient look of somebody being asked for directions twice.
{He} settled in for another one, without much joy.
{He} looked at me, then at the clock, and decided I was still there.
{He} brightened, which is what that kind does when you come back.
{He} had been hoping I’d ask something else, and it showed.
{He} leaned in, glad of the company.
{He} gave me the look people give the second question, which is less polite than the one they give the first.
{He} put down what {he} was doing, again.
